title: Problem_solving
summary:
Problem solving is the process of achieving a goal by overcoming obstacles, a frequent part of most activities. Problems in need of solutions range from simple personal tasks to complex issues in business and technical fields. Simple problem solving (SPS) addresses one issue, whereas complex problem solving (CPS) involves multiple interrelated obstacles.

Problems can be classified as well-defined (with specific obstacles and goals) or ill-defined (where the situation is troublesome but the resolution is unclear). One may also distinguish formal or fact-based problems requiring psychometric intelligence versus socio-emotional problems which depend on the changeable emotions of individuals or groups.

Solutions require sufficient resources and knowledge to attain the goal. Professionals such as lawyers, doctors, programmers, and consultants are largely problem solvers for issues requiring technical skills. There are many specialized problem-solving techniques in fields such as science, engineering, business, medicine, mathematics, computer science, philosophy, and social organization. Mental obstacles that prevent solutions include confirmation bias, mental set, and functional fixedness.

The process starts with problem finding and problem shaping, in which the problem is discovered and simplified. The next step is to generate possible solutions and evaluate them. Finally, a solution is selected to be implemented and verified. Problem solving has been defined as a higher-order cognitive process and intellectual function that requires the modulation and control of more routine or fundamental skills. Understanding the end goal and applicable rules is key, and sometimes a problem requires abstract thinking or a creative solution.
